answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can post jobs or claim rewards. A vertex in the trust graph gains influence only as its deposit backs completed work; proven fraud or duplicate claims burn that stake, while honest agents recover it after a dispute window. This does not make Sybils impossible, but it makes each extra identity costly: an attacker must tie up capital and risks losing it, rather than minting names for free. Even ember and karst accounts face the same price.
